title: Development of a revised conceptual framework of physical training for use in research and practice
authors: Jeffries AC, Marcora SM, Coutts AJ, Wallace L, McCall A, Impellizzeri FM
population: Not applicable (qualitative synthesis integrating the Banister and PerPot frameworks)
findings: Proposes 'training effects' as a measurable higher-order construct resulting from the combined effect of four possible responses (acute and chronic, positive and negative).
Explains training-effect measures (performance, physiological, subjective and other) and integrates a sport performance outcome continuum from improvement to overtraining.

Extends and defines the network of uni- and bidirectional linkages between individual and contextual factors and other constructs; applications include performance readiness and training tolerance when adapting training to individual responses.
limitations: Conceptual framework without empirical validation; no parameter values. Published online 2021-09-14; Europe PMC lists the 2022 print year.
implications: Model structure: keep separate stores for load (input), acute readiness/fatigue indicators and chronic performance measures, rather than one fitness-minus-fatigue scalar.
Include individual and contextual modifiers (age, sex, sleep, heat) as explicit moderators of response.

verification.notes: Crossref confirms title, Sports Med, 2021-09-14. Findings match abstract. The moderator examples in implications (age, sex, sleep, heat) are the engineers' application, not listed in the abstract.
